audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua southern coalition, sun-and-moon poem, five-kings execution, and city-destruction campaign, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Gibeonite treaty defense, five-king coalition, hailstones, Book of Jashar poem, ancient celestial language, cave imprisonment, foot-on-neck humiliation, sunset burial, and repeated total-destruction formulas.

verses.restored: It was, when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua captured Ai and devoted it to destruction—as he did to Jericho and its king, so he did to Ai and its king—and that inhabitants of Gibeon made peace with Israel and were in their midst,

familiar.text: Now it came to pass, when Adonizedec king of Jerusalem had heard how Joshua had taken Ai, and had utterly destroyed it; as he had done to Jericho and her king, so he had done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and were among them;

modern.text: Now Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction —doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king—and that the people of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living near them.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם כִּֽי לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת הָעַי֮ וַיַּחֲרִימָהּ֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה לִֽירִיחוֹ֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כֵּן עָשָׂ֥ה לָעַ֖י וּלְמַלְכָּ֑הּ וְכִ֨י הִשְׁלִ֜ימוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י גִבְעוֹן֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ בְּקִרְבָּֽם

verses.restored: that they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai and all its men were mighty.

familiar.text: That they feared greatly, because Gibeon was a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty.

modern.text: So Adoni-zedek and his people were greatly alarmed, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities; it was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty.

original.text: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עִ֤יר גְּדוֹלָה֙ גִּבְע֔וֹן כְּאַחַ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַמַּמְלָכָ֑ה וְכִ֨י הִ֤יא גְדוֹלָה֙ מִן הָעַ֔י וְכָל אֲנָשֶׁ֖יהָ גִּבֹּרִֽים

verses.restored: Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,

familiar.text: Wherefore Adonizedec king of Jerusalem sent unto Hoham king of Hebron, and unto Piram king of Jarmuth, and unto Japhia king of Lachish, and unto Debir king of Eglon, saying,

modern.text: Therefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִי צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶל הוֹהָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ חֶ֠בְרוֹן וְאֶל פִּרְאָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ יַרְמ֜וּת וְאֶל יָפִ֧יעַ מֶֽלֶךְ לָכִ֛ישׁ וְאֶל דְּבִ֥יר מֶֽלֶךְ עֶגְל֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, because it made peace with Joshua and children of Israel.

familiar.text: Come up unto me, and help me, that we may smite Gibeon: for it hath made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.

modern.text: “Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon, because they have made peace with Joshua and the Israelites.”

original.text: עֲלֽוּ אֵלַ֣י וְעִזְרֻ֔נִי וְנַכֶּ֖ה אֶת גִּבְע֑וֹן כִּֽי הִשְׁלִ֥ימָה אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Five kings of Amorite gathered and went up: king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, and king of Eglon, they and all their camps; they camped against Gibeon and fought against it.

familiar.text: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together, and went up, they and all their hosts, and encamped before Gibeon, and made war against it.

modern.text: So the five kings of the Amorites—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces and advanced with all their armies. They camped before Gibeon and made war against it.

original.text: וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ וַֽיַּעֲל֜וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֗י מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מֶֽלֶךְ חֶבְר֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ יַרְמוּת֙ מֶֽלֶךְ לָכִ֣ישׁ מֶֽלֶךְ עֶגְל֔וֹן הֵ֖ם וְכָל מַֽחֲנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל גִּבְע֔וֹן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at camp at Gilgal, saying, Do not slacken your hands from your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us and help us, for all kings of Amorite dwelling in hill country have gathered against us.

familiar.text: And the men of Gibeon sent unto Joshua to the camp to Gilgal, saying, Slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us: for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.

modern.text: Then the men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal: “Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us! Help us, because all the kings of the Amorites from the hill country have joined forces against us.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֣לָה לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל תֶּ֥רֶף יָדֶ֖יךָ מֵֽעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ עֲלֵ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מְהֵרָ֗ה וְהוֹשִׁ֤יעָה לָּ֨נוּ֙ וְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ כִּ֚י נִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ כָּל מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָהָֽר

verses.restored: Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all people of war with him, and all mighty men of strength.

familiar.text: So Joshua ascended from Gilgal, he, and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valour.

modern.text: So Joshua and his whole army, including all the mighty men of valor, came from Gilgal.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַל יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ מִן הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל ה֚וּא וְכָל עַ֤ם הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י הֶחָֽיִל

verses.restored: YHWH said to Joshua, Do not fear them, for into your hand I have given them; not a man from them shall stand before you.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee.

modern.text: The LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand against you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ אַל תִּירָ֣א מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י בְיָדְךָ֖ נְתַתִּ֑ים לֹֽא יַעֲמֹ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ מֵהֶ֖ם בְּפָנֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Joshua came upon them suddenly; all night he went up from Gilgal.

familiar.text: Joshua therefore came unto them suddenly, and went up from Gilgal all night.

modern.text: After marching all night from Gilgal, Joshua caught them by surprise.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פִּתְאֹ֑ם כָּל הַלַּ֕יְלָה עָלָ֖ה מִן הַגִּלְגָּֽל

verses.restored: YHWH confounded them before Israel, and he struck them with a great striking at Gibeon, pursued them by way of ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

familiar.text: And the LORD discomfited them before Israel, and slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chased them along the way that goeth up to Bethhoron, and smote them to Azekah, and unto Makkedah.

modern.text: And the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who defeated them in a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursued them along the ascent to Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

original.text: וַיְהֻמֵּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מַכָּֽה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בְּגִבְע֑וֹן וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ מַעֲלֵ֣ה בֵית חוֹרֹ֔ן וַיַּכֵּ֥ם עַד עֲזֵקָ֖ה וְעַד מַקֵּדָֽה

verses.restored: It was, as they fled from before Israel on descent of Beth-horon, that YHWH cast upon them great stones from heavens as far as Azekah, and they died; more died from hailstones than children of Israel killed with sword.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they fled from before Israel, and were in the going down to Bethhoron, that the LORD cast down great stones from heaven upon them unto Azekah, and they died: they were more which died with hailstones than they whom the children of Israel slew with the sword.

modern.text: As they fled before Israel along the descent from Beth-horon to Azekah, the LORD cast down on them large hailstones from the sky, and more of them were killed by the hailstones than by the swords of the Israelites.

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּנֻסָ֣ם מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֵ֞ם בְּמוֹרַ֤ד בֵּית חוֹרֹן֙ וַֽיהוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם עַד עֲזֵקָ֖ה וַיָּמֻ֑תוּ רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר מֵ֨תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Then Joshua spoke to YHWH on day YHWH gave Amorite before children of Israel, and he said before eyes of Israel: Sun, be still at Gibeon, and moon, in valley of Aijalon.

familiar.text: Then spake Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon.

modern.text: On the day that the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD in the presence of Israel: “O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”

original.text: אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם תֵּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בְּגִבְע֣וֹן דּ֔וֹם וְיָרֵ֖חַ בְּעֵ֥מֶק אַיָּלֽוֹן

verses.restored: Sun stood still and moon stayed until nation took vengeance upon its enemies. Is it not written in Scroll of Jashar? Sun stood in midst of heavens and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.

familiar.text: And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Is not this written in the book of Jasher? So the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.

modern.text: So the sun stood still and the moon stopped until the nation took vengeance upon its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? “So the sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed going down about a full day.”

original.text: וַיִּדֹּ֨ם הַשֶּׁ֜מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֣חַ עָמָ֗ד עַד יִקֹּ֥ם גּוֹי֙ אֹֽיְבָ֔יו הֲלֹא הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַשֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹא אָ֥ץ לָב֖וֹא כְּי֥וֹם תָּמִֽים

verses.restored: There was no day like it before it or after it, that YHWH listened to voice of a man, for YHWH fought for Israel.

familiar.text: And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.

modern.text: There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel.

original.text: וְלֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לְפָנָ֣יו וְאַחֲרָ֔יו לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ יְהוָ֖ה בְּק֣וֹל אִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֖ם לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to camp at Gilgal.

familiar.text: And Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, unto the camp to Gilgal.

modern.text: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal. The Victory at Makkedah

original.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ אֶל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּֽלָה

verses.restored: Those five kings fled and hid themselves in cave at Makkedah.

familiar.text: But these five kings fled, and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah.

modern.text: Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.

original.text: וַיָּנֻ֕סוּ חֲמֵ֖שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחָבְא֥וּ בַמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה

verses.restored: It was told to Joshua, saying, The five kings have been found hidden in cave at Makkedah.

familiar.text: And it was told Joshua, saying, The five kings are found hid in a cave at Makkedah.

modern.text: And Joshua was informed: “The five kings have been found; they are hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר נִמְצְאוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֔ים נֶחְבְּאִ֥ים בַּמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה

verses.restored: Joshua said, Roll great stones to mouth of cave and appoint men over it to guard them.

familiar.text: And Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, and set men by it for to keep them:

modern.text: So Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ גֹּ֛לּוּ אֲבָנִ֥ים גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֶל פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהַפְקִ֧ידוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לְשָׁמְרָֽם

verses.restored: But you, do not stand; pursue after your enemies and strike their rear. Do not let them enter their cities, for YHWH your Divine has given them into your hand.

familiar.text: And stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies, and smite the hindmost of them; suffer them not to enter into their cities: for the LORD your God hath delivered them into your hand.

modern.text: But you, do not stop there. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand.”

original.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ אַֽל תַּעֲמֹ֔דוּ רִדְפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיכֶ֔ם וְזִנַּבְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתָ֑ם אַֽל תִּתְּנ֗וּם לָבוֹא֙ אֶל עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֧י נְתָנָ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶֽם

verses.restored: It was, when Joshua and children of Israel finished striking them with a very great striking until they came to an end, and survivors who survived from them entered fortified cities,

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Joshua and the children of Israel had made an end of slaying them with a very great slaughter, till they were consumed, that the rest which remained of them entered into fenced cities.

modern.text: So Joshua and the Israelites continued to inflict a terrible slaughter until they had finished them off, and the remaining survivors retreated to the fortified cities.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה מְאֹ֖ד עַד תֻּמָּ֑ם וְהַשְּׂרִידִים֙ שָׂרְד֣וּ מֵהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָֽר

verses.restored: that all people returned to Joshua at camp at Makkedah in peace; no one sharpened/moved his tongue against any man of children of Israel.

familiar.text: And all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace: none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.

modern.text: The whole army returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah, and no one dared to utter a word against the Israelites.

original.text: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ֩ כָל הָעָ֨ם אֶל הַמַּחֲנֶ֧ה אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מַקֵּדָ֖ה בְּשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא חָרַ֞ץ לִבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְאִ֖ישׁ אֶת לְשֹׁנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Joshua said, Open mouth of cave and bring out to me those five kings from cave.

familiar.text: Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me out of the cave.

modern.text: Then Joshua said, “Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ פִּתְח֖וּ אֶת פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֗י אֶת חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן הַמְּעָרָֽה

verses.restored: They did so and brought out to him from cave those five kings: king of Jerusalem, king of Hebron, king of Jarmuth, king of Lachish, and king of Eglon.

familiar.text: And they did so, and brought forth those five kings unto him out of the cave, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

modern.text: So they brought the five kings out of the cave—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

translation_notes: Israel's treaty with Gibeon creates an obligation to defend the threatened Gibeonites, showing that the oath has practical force despite its deceptive origin.

The sun-and-moon passage is poetic ancient celestial language cited from the Scroll of Jashar, a lost source also named elsewhere. It should not be forced into modern astronomy or used to attack science.

Whether the poem describes prolonged daylight, cessation of celestial movement, silence, or another ancient image remains debated; the source-audited layer preserves its wording without pseudoscientific certainty.
Hailstones and sword are both agents of mass death. Miracle language does not make the violence ethically normative.
Placing feet on defeated kings' necks is ritualized domination and humiliation, not a model for leadership or treatment of captives.
The kings are executed, displayed, and removed by sunset in continuity with Deuteronomy's corpse law.
